issues.legal_issue: A writ court cannot resolve disputed technical questions by choosing between conflicting structural reports and authorizing work on that basis.
material_facts: The municipal authority’s Technical Advisory Committee found the buildings to be in a very dangerous condition and classified them as requiring immediate evacuation and demolition.
Structural assessments conflicted: some described the buildings as dangerous, while a report relied on by the tenant said repairs could extend the structure’s life.

The relied-on report described itself as a preliminary inspection, expressly stated that it was not a stability certificate, and warned that delay in major repairs could lead to partial or complete failure.
The High Court permitted removal of an adjoining wall based on that report, despite the conflicting technical assessments.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred by assessing the conflicting technical reports and permitting removal of the wall. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and dismissed the writ petition.
issues.legal_principle: In exercising its extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, a High Court does not adjudicate hotly disputed questions of fact or make a comparative assessment of conflicting technical reports to decide which is acceptable. No earlier cases are cited for this principle.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_order and conflicting_structural_reports and official_assessment_found_dangerous and relied_report_not_stability_certificate and writ_court_selected_technical_report

predicates.appeal_from_writ_order: An appeal challenges an order made by a court exercising writ jurisdiction.
predicates.conflicting_structural_reports: Different technical reports gave conflicting assessments of a structure’s condition or safety.
predicates.official_assessment_found_dangerous: A technical body acting for a public authority found the structure dangerous.
predicates.relied_report_not_stability_certificate: The report relied on to support work on the structure stated that it was not a stability certificate.
predicates.writ_court_selected_technical_report: The writ court assessed conflicting technical reports and relied on one of them to permit work on the structure.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a writ order, structural reports conflict, an official assessment finds the structure dangerous, the relied-on report is not a stability certificate, and the writ court selects between the reports, the output is that the writ order is set aside and the writ petition is dismissed.
